title: Uber Michelangelo — end-to-end ML in production
what: Uber built Michelangelo to standardize data management, training, evaluation, deployment, prediction, and monitoring. UberEATS ETA was one published production use case.
lesson: Treat an ML model as one component in a lifecycle. Reproducibility, feature consistency, deployment, A/B testing, and live monitoring matter as much as training.

title: Air Canada chatbot — wrong policy, real liability
what: A Canadian tribunal found Air Canada liable after its website chatbot gave incorrect information about bereavement fares and a customer relied on it.
lesson: A production chatbot is a publishing/decision surface. Grounding, policy consistency, monitoring, escalation, and accountability are controls—not optional extras.

title: Amazon recruiting model — historical bias
what: Reuters reported that Amazon abandoned an experimental recruiting system after it learned patterns that disadvantaged women for some technical roles.
lesson: Historical labels can encode social bias. Accuracy alone is insufficient; subgroup evaluation, data review, and governance are necessary.

title: Zillow Offers — forecasting uncertainty became business risk
what: Zillow said it would wind down Zillow Offers after concluding that home-price forecasting unpredictability was greater than anticipated and created excessive earnings and balance-sheet volatility.
lesson: Model error becomes business risk when decisions scale. Evaluate uncertainty, downside exposure, operating constraints, and rollback/exit conditions.
